lessons: Topic = a hidden feature of a real, named product people know, with the mechanism as the payoff (scroll.engineer's named-product posts reach up to 187x its median). English: famous global cars and bikes. Indonesian: what Indonesians ride (Beat, Vario, Scoopy, NMAX, Avanza, Xpander, Innova). Every claim about the product needs 2 sources, the maker's own first.
Title = brand + surprising capability + one emoji (👀 🤯 😳), under 70 characters, never 'how X works' ('Honda scooters switch off their engine at every red light 🤯').
Frame 1 is already moving: a cold open mid-action or the part flying together (<Engine explode>), with the hook's key number or words on screen; never a slow push-in on an empty shot.

Animation language (docs/styles.md): 2-3 shots per scene (cut: true), X-ray focus and a <Callout> on the part the narration names, one slow-motion moment with <TimeTag> on the moment the episode is about.

Shares are our missing signal: 0 shares on 37 Instagram posts, and views stall at about 130. Instagram says sends per reach is one of its strongest signals for reaching non-followers. Send lines name a person ('Send this to someone who rides an NMAX'); question lines are answered in one word ('yes or no?').
Frame 1 names the product on screen (a Callout with brand and model on the whole vehicle), so the hook reads with the sound off.
Indonesian Instagram lags most (1,706 views in 7 days against 11,362 on Indonesian YouTube): Indonesian titles lead with the bike or car Indonesians own (NMAX, Vario, PCX, Avanza).

Hook that holds (YouTube % watched): flip what the viewer believes about their own vehicle, then ask ('A diesel has no spark plugs. So what lights it?' 55-84%; 'Pressing the clutch doesn't connect anything' 60-72%). The 'X times a second' number hook held only 37-58%: use it in at most 2 of 14.
Under 58 s in both languages: our longest video (56 s) was watched least (35%). Answer the hook's question by scene 4; keep the last scenes for the catch and the closing line.
English and Indonesian use different looks (strategy.json looks) so the two channels never upload the same picture: Indonesian YouTube got 7 views on 4 posts, likely treated as reused content.

goal.note: combined views of all four accounts (both YouTube channels, both Instagram accounts) in one week, from data/snapshot.json
